findings.title: Rescheduling a booking passes `immediateDelete = true`, bypassing deferred cancellation and leaving orphaned reminder rows
findings.body: When cancelling reminders for `originalRescheduledBooking`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is `true`, it immediately sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` to SendGrid instead of marking `cancelled: true` for the cron job, and then returns early without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row from the database (since rescheduling only marks the original booking `CANCELLED` rather than deleting it). Consequently, rescheduled bookings still immediately consume SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellations limit (for up to 72 hours), and the `WorkflowReminder` record remains in the database where subsequent workflow edits can mark it `cancelled: true` and cause the cron job to attempt a duplicate cancellation.

findings.title: Single failure in `remindersToCancel` loop skips remaining cancellations and leaves already-cancelled reminders in DB
findings.body: The `try/catch` block and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` wrap the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop rather than each individual reminder. Because `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that only executes when `await Promise.all(...)` is reached, if `client.request` throws for any reminder in the batch: (1) all remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped, and (2) reminders earlier in the loop that were already cancelled in SendGrid are never deleted from the database. On the next cron run, those already-cancelled reminders will be queried again and `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be called with the same `batch_id`, which SendGrid rejects as a duplicate, permanently wedging the loop on every subsequent run.

findings.title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never set in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`
findings.body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (which only configures `@sendgrid/mail`'s internal client instance) but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the `@sendgrid/client` singleton (unlike `emailReminderManager.ts`). When the cron job calls `client.request` to cancel scheduled sends at `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` (or create batches at `/v3/mail/batch`), the client has no `Authorization` header configured and will fail with `401 Unauthorized` unless `emailReminderManager.ts` happened to be imported in the same process beforehand.

findings.title: Deferring cancellation to the 15-minute cron job when `scheduledDate` is already within 1 hour allows imminent emails to be sent
findings.body: When a booking is cancelled or rescheduled, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only sets `cancelled: true` on the `WorkflowReminder` and relies on the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job (which runs every 15 minutes) to cancel reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled when the reminder's `scheduledDate` is already less than 15–25 minutes away (SendGrid does not guarantee cancellation less than 10 minutes before `send_at`, and the next cron tick may occur after `scheduledDate`), the reminder email will be sent before the cron job cancels it. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is already within the next hour should be cancelled in SendGrid and deleted immediately.

findings.title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with cascade deletes and response completion
findings.body: In `workflows.tsx` (lines 212–218, 376–382, 519–525, 574–580), `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 485–493), `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 966–972), and `bookings.tsx` (lines 488–494), the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without `await` or `Promise.all`. In `workflows.delete` (line 220) and `workflows.update` step deletion (line 527), `workflow.deleteMany` / `workflowStep.delete` runs immediately and cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (or `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` when `referenceId` is null) is still running, causing `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` to fail with `P2025` (record not found). In the booking handlers, returning the HTTP response before awaiting these promises risks terminating the database updates and external API calls prematurely in serverless environments.
